question.question: Which of the following statements about L1 and L2 regularization are correct?

options.text: L1 regularization tends to produce sparse weight vectors, effectively performing feature selection
L2 regularization shrinks weights towards zero but rarely sets them exactly to zero
L1 regularization has a unique global minimum for convex loss functions, while L2 can have multiple minima
The L1 penalty term is differentiable everywhere, making gradient-based optimization straightforward
Elastic Net regularization combines L1 and L2 penalties to handle correlated features better than either alone

question.explanation: L1 regularization (Lasso) produces sparsity by driving some weights exactly to zero, performing feature selection. L2 regularization (Ridge) shrinks weights proportionally but rarely produces exact zeros. L1 is non-differentiable at zero (making optimization trickier, not easier). For convex loss functions, L2 has a unique minimum due to strict convexity, while L1 can have multiple minima along flat regions. Elastic Net combines both penalties to handle correlated features more effectively.
